action_items: Testing agent already applied a fix to /app/frontend/src/components/legal/LegalDoc.jsx (chip regex upper bound 110 → 200). Main agent should sanity-check and keep this change. Rationale below in critical_code_review_comments.
critical_code_review_comments: FIXED by testing agent: LegalDoc.jsx renderInline() regex /(\*\*[^*]+\*\*)|(\[[^\][]{3,110}\])/g only matched bracketed fill-in fields up to 110 chars. The Terms doc section 17 contains '[have counsel define any agreed carve-outs, such as fraud, wilful misconduct, payment obligations, confidentiality, or indemnification]' (~131 chars) which was leaking as plain visible text — exposing the string 'have counsel' that the review-request explicitly flagged as internal-only checklist leakage. Bumped the upper bound to 200. After fix: chip now rendered correctly (haveCounselInChip=True, total chips 6→7); no other brackets exceed the new limit.

Iteration-1 open items still worth main-agent attention (unchanged): in-memory rate-limit keyed by request.client.host behind ingress sees a shared IP; consider X-Forwarded-For. Pydantic EmailStr would simplify validation in server.py.

BackersBand GSAP: scroll_into_view_if_needed times out on the moving element because the marquee is permanently animating — this is cosmetic to the test only, not a bug. Verified via computedStyle(transform) deltas instead.

No real price numbers found on home, /pricing, llms.txt, JSON-LD, or sitemap. Legal pages correctly noindex,nofollow and excluded from sitemap while listed in llms.txt as drafts — matches checklist intent.

rca of the issue: Single minor leak found & fixed. RCA: LegalDoc.jsx fill-in-chip regex upper bound was 110 chars but termsDoc section 17 contains a 131-char bracketed drafter instruction '[have counsel define any agreed carve-outs...]'. Repro: GET /terms, document.body.innerText.includes('have counsel') returned true pre-fix. Fix: raised regex upper bound to 200 so all current bracketed fields render as chips. Post-fix verified: that bracket is now a span[title] chip and body text no longer leaks the phrase outside of a chip.
